environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 8 application deployed on Azure App Service with Azure SQL Database. Database connection uses per-request SESSION_CONTEXT injection via EF Core interceptor that sets tenant_id from JWT claim. PostgreSQL-style RLS is approximated using SQL Server security policies: a SECURITY POLICY [dbo].[TenantFilterPolicy] with a FILTER PREDICATE and BLOCK PREDICATE using function [dbo].[fn_tenant_access_predicate] that reads SESSION_CONTEXT(N'tenant_id') and compares against the row's tenant_id column. The policy is created WITH (STATE = ON, SCHEMABINDING = OFF). The database user (app_restricted_user) has DENY on ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY and cannot modify or disable the RLS policy. The interceptor is registered in DbContext configuration via AddInterceptors() and executes sp_set_session_context @key=N'tenant_id', @value=@tenantId, @read_only=1 before each command batch.

config.db_user: app_restricted_user with limited SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on documents table only
config.session_context_injection: EF Core IDbCommandInterceptor sets sp_set_session_context @read_only=1 per request
config.db_permissions: DENY ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY TO app_restricted_user
config.network: App Service VNet integration, SQL private endpoint
config.auth: Azure AD B2C JWT with tenant_id claim
